Why OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX's Cursor Are All Building Their Own GitHub

From dev.to•Yesterday•13m read time

OpenAI, Anthropic, and Cursor (now owned by SpaceX) are each building their own alternatives to GitHub because AI coding agents generate far more commits and pushes than Git hosting was designed for. Anthropic's daily merges rose from about 2,500 in May to over 30,000 in September, prompting it to replace Git for its monorepo with an in-house system called Scion, which it reports uses about 200x less CPU and memory than its old Git mirroring infrastructure. OpenAI built a Rust-based Git backend called Pando that cut median push latency by about 80% and reached 99.99% merge reliability, and is acquiring Pierre Computer to bring Code Storage into Codex. Cursor's Origin, built into its editor, is in early beta for paid plans and syncs two-way with GitHub. An independent tracker logged 257 incidents at GitHub between May 2025 and April 2026 while it migrates to Azure, and GitHub says it has added 3+ million CPU cores since the August 17 outage.
